summary: A two-story octagonal lighthouse on a Lynn Canal rock, lit in 1906 for Skagway shipping and manned until 1973; now leased to a preservation group.

access.note: Coast Guard property; Lighthouse Friends lists grounds, dwelling and tower as closed; USLHS lists it as not open to the public; seen from passing ferries; tours run by an operator in Haines and Skagway.

notes_for_editor: Core facts rest on the NRHP nomination, Lighthouse Friends (secondary; includes logbook quotes and 1910 letter as relayed) and the USLHS roster. Primary corroboration is thin: Lighthouse Board annual reports 1905-1907 for Alaska were not located in the corpus (corpus holds only 1899-1901 LHB volumes). The 1933 Bulletin article on a keeper's death is unreadable OCR; only the index entry (itself OCR-damaged: 'Eldrod ... unblown') was cited. The 1918 Bulletin rescue (Shoemaker, 3-4 Nov) was seen only in garbled OCR and left out. NRHP 'visible about 15 miles' does not say statute or nautical. Roster (USLHS) has a 1941-1960 gap; Lighthouse Friends adds Harry E. Frey (at least 1950) and Charles Chase 1918, not in USLHS; not used. 1921 Erickson incident and 1910 loss rely on Lighthouse Friends quoting station records. Names of postwar Coast Guard people deliberately not used in the story. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the LHB 1901 list of eleven localities is a repeat of the Board's earlier statement (printed before a Dec 1899 Treasury letter), not a 1901 decision. The 1930-35 index entry is OCR-damaged ('unblown'); story no longer guesses the word. Lease of April 2020 was for five years; current status unknown.
